app_summary: An online shop selling astronomy products, based on the OpenTelemetry Demo. It is built with polyglot microservices (Go, Java, .NET, Python, Node.js, Rust, ...) communicating via gRPC and HTTP behind an Envoy frontend-proxy, with Kafka for asynchronous order processing and Valkey as cart store. Supported Operations: View product catalog, Receive product recommendations and ads, Add item to cart, Checkout with selected items, Currency conversion, Process payment, Generate shipping quotes, Send order confirmation emails

final_report.root_cause: The frontend Service port was configured with a non-standard port name ('tcp-service') (and the same pattern appears across multiple backend services). This non-conventional port naming prevented components that rely on service port names for protocol detection/configuration (e.g., Envoy/frontend proxy or service-mesh/proxy generation) from creating correct listeners/routes to the frontend. As a result, upstream callers (frontend-proxy, frontend-web) intermittently received TCP connection refusals (ECONNREFUSED / gRPC UNAVAILABLE) when attempting to reach the frontend pod IPs even though the frontend process itself was running and listening on 8080. The immediate manifest-level misconfiguration (misnamed port) is the direct cause; this likely became visible after a change (service port naming change or a proxy/mesh version/config change) that made the proxy enforcement of named ports stricter.
